thread:
anya: flagging a spike: ~90 leads in the past 10h landed with no owner because enrichment webhooks stalled. reps are seeing gaps in their queue.

lucas: saw the anomaly on dashboards. our RR assign workflow only runs on enrichment.complete event; if that never fires the lead stays ownerless.

olivia: that's rough. A quick mitigation: automatic soft-assign into an "unverified" routing pool after a timeout, visible to SDRs but blocked from SF sync. That keeps human follow-ups possible without polluting CRM.

sam: agree. Principle: never let a lead sit unowned > 1 hour. Prefer much lower (1015m) for inbound. Proposal: fallback assign after 8 minutes of no enrichment, mark enrichment_status=timed_out, set routing_note='Fallback:PendingEnrich', and set crm.sync_allowed=false.

anya: short-term sounds good. long-term we should also harden enrichment (retries/backoff) and surface a real-time alert to ops when webhook 5xx rate > 15% in a 5m window.

lucas: technical nit: if we soft-assign to a real user it will cause notifications and confusion. make the fallback a queue user (e.g., 'Queue:Inbound-Fallback') or a dedicated placeholder owner id. that also simplifies reassignment when enrichment completes.

olivia: plan for HubSpot workflow change (staging -> prod):
```
# simplified workflow
- on lead created: start enrichment attempts (3 retries, immediate)
- if enrichment fails and elapsed >= 8m:
    set owner = 'Queue:Inbound-Fallback'
    set enrichment_status = 'timed_out'
    set crm_sync_allowed = 'false'
    set routing_note = 'Fallback:PendingEnrich'
- when enrichment completes later:
    update lead properties and re-run normal owner assignment (if needed)
```

sam: can we also add a middleware check so that even if owner != null, we skip SF push when crm_sync_allowed == false? that avoids changing push behavior everywhere.

lucas: yes. middleware change is minimal: honor crm_sync_allowed flag before enqueuing push. i'll scope that as a configuration toggle so we can flip it quickly.

anya: we need a short SLA blurb for sales/SDR comms: "Inbound routing: owners assigned within 10 minutes; if enrichment delays, lead will be placed in a fallback queue and not pushed to Salesforce until enrichment completes." i'll draft and circulate.

olivia: testing plan: replay failed-enrich webhook events in staging, verify fallback assign after 8m, verify crm_sync_allowed blocks SF push, ensure re-assign on enrichment arrival. will attach logs/screenshots.

sales-ops-bot: FYI — created ticket SO-1429 to update SDR playbook with the fallback queue behavior.

sam: ops alerting: add a PagerDuty for enrich-service 5xx spike, and a grafana panel for ownerless_leads_count. threshold: >30 in 1h -> pager.

lucas: another small improvement: exponential retry with jitter before we consider fallback. current retries are aggressive. suggest: retries at 15s, 45s, 2m, 6m then fallback at 8m. reduces cascade when enrichment has transient hiccups.

olivia: agree. I'll implement the backoff schedule in enrichment worker config in staging.

anya: timeline and owners:
- olivia: implement hubspot workflow + backoff in staging today
- lucas: middleware flag to block SF pushes based on crm_sync_allowed today
- sam: alerting + metrics dashboard update today
- anya: sales messaging + SDR playbook update (SO-1429) by EOD

lucas: quick Q 14 do we want to set a TTL for fallback owners so they auto-release after X hours if enrichment never completes? prevents perpetual queues.

olivia: yes, set auto-release at 72h and notify sales-ops weekly for any remainders.

sam: I'll add a runbook entry: how to manually reassign, how to force-sync to SF if enrichment is known good, and rollback steps for workflow changes.

anya: sounds good. if staging tests pass we'll promote to prod tomorrow morning with a short smoke-test window. thanks team. :rocket:

lucas: posting a small PR for middleware change in a bit.

olivia: staging screenshots incoming.

hubspot-sync-bot: enrichment service reported 18% 5xx over 5m window at 2026-03-20T10:12Z. linked ENG-7241.

anya: closing: keep this thread updated with staging verification. we'll run a quick retrospective next week if we see repeated fallbacks.

lucas: thanks everyone.
